originalOutcome: A stranger can install Lenny into a non-empty repository, say “set up Lenny,” receive a sensible three-seat implementation council and successfully conduct one small plan to a verified merge-ready branch.

criteria.text: A Codex user can safely install Lenny into a non-empty repository without overwriting existing instructions or skills.
The user can say “set up Lenny” and receive a repository-grounded .lenny/profile.md plus the default three-seat software implementation council.
Lenny Doctor reports actionable installation, configuration, verification and Codex-host health.
Standard and high-stakes implementation runs select deterministic, tested review requirements.
Automated tests and CI prove clean install, non-empty install, idempotent update, rollback, diagnostics and the setup contract.
The public repository has semantic version metadata, release documentation and a tested update path while personal councils remain excluded.

One temporary non-empty Codex repository installs Lenny, completes setup and Doctor, conducts one small plan through the default council and frozen gates, pushes its feature branch to a distinct remote and passes the strict merge-ready interlock against the remote-advertised tip.
